quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black lettering. These signs tell you the rules of the road. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: If your motorcycle begins to wobble, you should:

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle gradually.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble. This makes it worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle to slow down. Lean forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can.

questions.question: How often should a motorcycle operator check their mirrors?

options.text: More often than the amount time spent looking ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Frequently
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often. This helps you see hazards behind you.

questions.question: Where is the greatest potential for conflict between motorcycle operators and other drivers?
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections have the most crashes between motorcycles and other vehicles. Be extra careful when approaching and going through intersections.

questions.question: In a normal turn:

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should not.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should not.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, lean the motorcycle and your body together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while you stay upright.

questions.question: The primary source of information about your motorcycle should come from:
questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual.
questions.explanation: Use the owner's manual as your main source for information about your motorcycle. Read it before you ride for the first time.

questions.question: If you are not traveling slowly enough when shifting into a lower gear, the:

options.text: Motorcycle could lurch and the rear tire could skid.
Engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle could lurch and the rear tire could skid.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear too fast will cause the motorcycle to jerk and the rear tire may skid.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride a little more slowly than usual.
Ride a little faster than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride a little more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle sits lower with a passenger on it. Ride slower than usual, especially around curves and bumps. The extra weight means your motorcycle needs more time to speed up, slow down, and stop. Keep a bigger space between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: To lower the chance of a crash, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Be prepared to react to hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope another driver sees you.
questions.explanation: To stay safe, make sure other drivers can see you and know what you are doing. Use your signals and position your bike correctly. Keep space between you and other vehicles. Watch for hazards ahead and be ready to react.

questions.question: When it starts raining, it is usually best to:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off to the side of the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: In wet conditions, do not ride down the center of the lane. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track is often best, but this can change based on traffic and conditions.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may only make them tailgate you faster.

questions.question: What is a major effect of drinking alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: Your body works more slowly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows down your body and mind. It damages both physical and mental function.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride?

options.text: In the center of your lane.
On the left side of your lane.
On the right side of your lane.
Move side to side as the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may make the other driver merge back too soon.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When you slow down somewhere drivers won't expect it.
When a stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you slow down somewhere drivers won't expect it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are harder to see than car brake lights. Flash your brake light before slowing down in unexpected places, like the middle of a block or near an alley. This helps other drivers notice you.

questions.question: Which surface does NOT have poor traction?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings all have poor traction. Dry pavement provides good traction.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: After mounting your motorcycle, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Make sure the mirrors are clean.
Check that the clutch works smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the fuel supply valve.
questions.explanation: After mounting your motorcycle, check the clutch, throttle, horn, and brakes. Clean and adjust the mirrors. Keep the fuel supply valve open.

questions.question: What is true about a windshield?

options.text: It works as well as a face shield.
It does not fully protect your eyes from wind.
It is required on all motorcycles.
Use it only on windy days.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not fully protect your eyes from wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield does not provide enough protection for your eyes. You still need goggles or a face shield for proper eye protection.

questions.question: What should a passenger do when riding on a motorcycle?

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Put their feet on the muffler.
Get on after you start the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on after you start the engine.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to get on only after the engine is started. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold onto your waist, hips, or belt. They must keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: What is true about brightly-colored helmets?

options.text: They may help others see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may help others see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a brightly-colored helmet. It protects you in a crash and helps other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: A face shield should:

options.text: Give you a clear view to both sides.
Block air from passing through it.
Be tight enough so glasses cannot fit under it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a clear view to both sides.
questions.explanation: A good face shield must be clear and free of scratches, resist damage, give clear views to both sides, fasten securely, allow air to pass through, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: Once a motorcycle helmet has been in a crash, it should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Replaced.
questions.explanation: Always replace any helmet that has been worn during a crash.

questions.question: When changing lanes, riders should:

options.text: Use only their mirrors to check for other vehicles.
Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
Brake hard to let vehicles in their blind spot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Move to the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles may weave over rain grooves or bridge gratings, but this is usually not dangerous. Stay relaxed and go straight ahead at a steady speed. Weaving back and forth will only make it more dangerous.

questions.question: Rain suits:

options.text: Are not needed because motorcycles should not ride in rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not balloon when riding.
questions.explanation: Good quality rain suits for motorcycles resist tearing and ballooning when you ride at high speeds.
